title: Lamb Keema Matar
subtitle: A quick North Indian mince curry with peas and warm spices
excerpt: Spiced minced lamb cooked down into a dry, fragrant mince with peas stirred through at the end. Ready in 30 minutes and good with rice or chapatis.
sourceNotes: Keema matar is a staple of everyday North Indian and Pakistani home cooking; this version draws on Punjabi and Mughal traditions.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to three months. Defrost overnight and reheat in a dry pan over a medium heat.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles and triples easily in a wide, heavy pan. Cook the mince in batches if the pan is not wide enough.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook up to two days ahead and refrigerate. The flavour improves overnight. Reheat with a splash of water.

content.text: Keema matar is one of the fastest curries to cook. The key step is cooking out the mince until all its liquid has gone. A wet keema is flat in flavour. Drive off the water first, then let the spices fry in the fat that remains.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over a medium to high heat. Add the onion and fry for 10 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden brown.
Add the garlic and ginger. Stir for two minutes. Add the cumin, coriander, turmeric and chilli powder. Stir for one minute.
Add the lamb mince and break it up with a spoon. Cook over a high heat for five minutes, breaking up any lumps, until no pink remains.
Keep cooking over a high heat, stirring often, until all the liquid has cooked off and the mince begins to fry in its own fat. This takes eight to 10 minutes. Do not rush this step.
Add the chopped tomatoes and salt. Stir and cook for five minutes until the tomatoes soften and break down into the mince.
Stir in the frozen peas and cook for three minutes until heated through.
Sprinkle over the garam masala and a squeeze of lemon. Taste and adjust salt. Scatter with fresh coriander and serve.

items.symptom: The keema is wet and lacks flavour.
items.cause: The mince was not cooked long enough after browning.
items.fix: The liquid must fully evaporate before the tomatoes go in. Keep the heat high and stir often until the mince fries, not stews.

items.cause: They were added too late, or not fried long enough.
items.fix: Fry the ground spices in the oil with the onion mix for at least a full minute before the mince goes in.

items.cause: They were added too early and cooked for too long.
items.fix: Add frozen peas in the last three minutes only. They need just enough time to heat through.
